page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the ARM64 architecture and powered by a 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs. It features 128 GiB of system memory, providing a 2 GiB per vCPU ratio optimized for core-dense workloads. The hardware runs on a KVM hypervisor without simultaneous multithreading. Hardware support includes AES encryption instructions, while x86-specific extensions such as AVX are not present. The server does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and providing a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel compute capabilities. The instance scores in the upper tier for multi-core stress-ng tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-block cached memory bandwidth achieves high throughput, and Redis SET throughput reaches 84.36 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance in stress-ng single-core tests and weaker throughput in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. PassMark CPU tests, static web serving, and small-to-medium model LLM inference speeds remain within standard mid-range bands.

The 2 GiB per vCPU configuration offers high resource density for multi-core scaling rather than memory-bound operations. The absence of integrated local storage necessitates reliance on external block storage, which can impact local I/O intensive pipelines. Overall, the instance is well suited for multi-threaded application servers, high-concurrency Redis caching layers, microservices architectures, parallel compilation, and general batch processing workloads designed for ARM64.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6r.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-core 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra ARM64 processor, paired with 128 GiB of RAM, providing 2 GiB per vCPU. Operating on KVM with dedicated cores, it lacks local storage and bundled GPUs, relying on external network-attached volumes and a 16 Gbps baseline network interface. Performance benchmarks reveal strong multi-core processing capabilities, notable small-cache memory bandwidth, and high Redis SET throughput of 84.36 million operations per second. However, single-core speeds and single-threaded decompression metrics remain in average-to-lower tiers. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers efficiency for core-dense parallel workloads rather than memory-heavy software. It is best suited for multi-threaded backend services, distributed caching layers, parallel data processing, and microservice architectures built for native ARM execution.
